tips.text: Approaching or viewing the Eiffel Tower from Trocadero provides one of the best and most iconic views of the landmark.
Visiting the observatory deck at night offers breathtaking views of the Paris skyline.
You can take the elevator down from the 2nd floor to the 1st floor.
Be aware of petition scammers and bracelet vendors operating near the Eiffel Tower.
Expect potentially long queue times when trying to travel back down from the top level.

tips.text: Purchase admission tickets exclusively through the official ticket office to avoid counterfeit tickets.
Opening hours are 9:00 am to 6:30 pm for the Palace, 12:00 pm to 6:30 pm for the Estate of Trianon, 7:00 am to 5:30 pm for the Gardens, and 7:00 am to 8:30 pm for the Park.
The fountains are shut down for part of the year due to cold temperatures to protect the pipes.
To reach Versailles from Paris, take RER Line C or alternative lines such as L, U, or N.
Keep your train ticket after arriving at the station, as you will need it to exit.
For getting around the estate and gardens, options include renting a bike, taking the paid tram (which is cheaper than golf carts), or renting a golf cart.

tips.text: The fountain is free to view from the upper area, but closer access to the basin costs 2 euros with a quick-moving queue system.
Visiting early in the morning or before dawn, particularly in winter, allows you to avoid heavy crowds and view the floodlit statues in peace.
Keep a close watch on your belongings near the fountain, as backpack theft has been reported in the immediate area.
Check the live web camera feed of Trevi Fountain before heading out to gauge current crowd levels.
